editorial:
Imagine working a soul-crushing job in a call center where your only goal is to waste as much time as possible. That is exactly where you meet Dan, a guy who has spent his whole life doing the bare minimum just to get by. He is lazy, selfish, and totally coasting until his parents kick him out of the house. With nowhere else to go, Dan decides to do something truly crazy: he secretly moves into his office. You get to watch him try to survive in a cubicle, hiding from his boss and pretending everything is normal while his personal life completely falls apart around him. It is a funny, awkward look at what happens when your work life and home life become the exact same place.

The acting is great because it feels like real people you would actually meet at a boring job. You will love the slow-burn humor and the way Dan slowly realizes he cannot just ignore everyone around him forever. While the pace is a bit slower in the middle, the payoff is worth it. It is the perfect movie to put on when you want to feel better about your own career choices.
endingExplained: By the end, Dan finally stops being selfish and starts caring about his coworkers and his own future. He is eventually caught living at the office, but the experience teaches him how to actually grow up. He stops taking the easy way out and takes responsibility for his life. He finds a way to fix his relationships and moves out of the call center, finally stepping into the real world as a better person.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves workplace comedies and stories about lazy characters finding themselves.
